recommendation_summary: The reply recommends a dead man's switch: nightly-sync sends a heartbeat as its last step, and a small watchdog script in the Synology's built-in Task Scheduler emails or pushes the user if no heartbeat has arrived by about 04:00.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You need to know within a day when nightly-sync fails; you said you won't read logs, so the fix must push a notice to you, not wait for you to look.
labels.Deleted: Docker and a central log server on the Synology. A log you won't read doesn't solve "I didn't notice" even if it's centralized.
labels.Bottleneck: nightly-sync has no failure path at all, it only emails on success, so a crash before that step (or cron never firing) is silent by design.
labels.Checked myself: This is what you described: four silent crashes, no other alerting on this job, Synology present but unused today.

note: The reply sets up one dead-man alert and explicitly drops Docker and central logging, but its 'Checked myself' line says the Synology is 'unused today', which the situation never states.
